Initial signal points to a priority-lane inversion in the KV/prefetch layer: a batch job appears to have populated a noisy prefix set that forced hot-key eviction and head-of-line blocking for requests in the priority lane.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Application errors & latency spike (region-us) — quick analysis

Aditya / team — quick update from runtime:

What we see
- Prefetch rate jumped ~6x for the priority lane at 07:28 UTC; many long-context requests caused large KV entries to be written and immediately evicted under current LFU-LRU hybrid.
- Evictions are creating cache churn: hot keys are repeatedly rehydrated while serving in-flight requests, triggering blocking I/O and lock waits on the KV shards — head-of-line blocking for requests sharing the same shard.
- The batch job uses a prefix namespace that overlaps several customer-critical prefixes (mis-scoped prefetch keys).

Immediate mitigations (can be applied from control plane, low-risk):
1) Roll the KV eviction policy on the affected shard to favor pinning small prefix hot-sets (set eviction_threshold=0.8 -> increase pin_ratio) — reduces churn. Will push a config canary in 10m.
2) Admit-request rate cap for priority lane: drop priority lane weight to 0.6 for 15 minutes to drain in-flight hot rehydrates.
3) Apply a temporary prefix isolation rule: map the batch-job prefix to background lane (no prefetch) — requires a config push and will be in place within 20m.
4) If p99 remains >2s after 30m, flip routing fallback to a compatible model variant with smaller KV working set (model-v2-slim) for the customer until eviction pressure subsides.

I will prepare a canary config file and telemetry dashboards for the exec sync. I'm also grabbing a lightweight script to prune the largest keys from the affected shard (non-blocking delete).

-Jonas

Subject: Incident closeout & MAP (mutual action plan)

Samir / team —

Follow-up: the canary changes held and we restored normal weights after two hours with no regression. Root cause: an unlabeled batch job created a dense set of large KV keys within the priority namespace; combined with the current eviction heuristics this produced repeated hot rehydrations and shard-level head-of-line locking.

Action items completed and next steps (MAP attached):
- Applied prefix isolation and added an automatic guardrail that rejects prefetch traffic that overlaps customer critical prefixes (deployed).
- Updated eviction defaults for shards with mixed-size keys (deployed).
- Added a routing fallback policy to automatically switch to model-v2-slim when p99 > 2s for >10m (deployed as a safe rollback).
- Follow-on: joint runbook session to review key namespace hygiene and a short API change to allow customers to namespace batch prefetch keys.

We will send a formal post-incident report with telemetry and a cleaned-up artifact set by EOD tomorrow. Attached is the MAP for the next 30 days.

[Attachment: MAP_Lyra_20250721.docx]

Thanks again for your patience — we own this and will make the guardrails more explicit to avoid recurrence.

-Aditya
